correctness.rationale: C: z=|axial cosine| is uniform [0,1]; support-function subtraction gives W/r=a+max(a,kz), a=√(1−z²), k=h/r. Split at z0=1/√(1+k²), and for k>1 at zm=k/√(1+k²). Inverse-Jacobian branches C,B,A give exact nonnegative piecewise density integrating to 1. Global minima/maxima switch simultaneously at k=√3; L,U formulas agree by direct extremization. At lower edge, if k<√3 density tends to zero, whereas for k≥√3 its right limit is (k/2+k/(k²−1))/r>0. Thus edge law identifies regime and reconstructs (r,h). In strict support-ratio regime both broad and slender solutions exist, unique within their branch. Independent direct directional grid and numerical quadrature confirmed normalization for k=.4,1,1.3,√3,2.2,5; proof is analytic for all ratios.
